interpretation.claim: Tests whether acceleration-scale profiles fitted to the lower-quality SPARC Q=3 challenge sample are consistent with the already-certified Q<=2 profiles under the same declared nuisance treatment.
not_claimed: proof of EMRF or any acceleration law
interpretation.prior_exposure: The public SPARC catalogue and Q<=2 outcomes were previously examined. No repository result or analysis of the Q=3 profile was found before this contract was committed.

include: SPARC catalogue quality flag Q equals 3
catalogue inclination is at least 30 degrees
rotation-curve file has at least three rows after point filtering
point_filter: observed velocity is greater than zero
population.error_treatment: Observed velocity uncertainty is floored at 1 km/s, matching the certified Q<=2 pipeline.
population.exclusions: No galaxy satisfying every frozen rule may be removed after outcomes are computed. Missing or failed targets must be reported and make the confirmatory result incomplete.

analysis.observable: SPARC rotation velocity in the catalogue velocity coordinate
analysis.objective: Gaussian velocity residual sum plus declared nuisance-parameter penalties
nuisance_parameters_per_galaxy: log10 stellar mass-to-light ratio with centre 0.5 and width 0.1 dex
distance factor with catalogue uncertainty and a minimum fractional width of 0.02
inclination with catalogue uncertainty and a minimum width of 1 degree
analysis.unknown_covariance: Radial covariance is unavailable and will not be invented.
analysis.optimizer: The certified bounded multi-start least-squares profile with analytic Jacobian and continuation.
analysis.scan_order_check: Repeat each profile in reverse grid order.

hypotheses.criterion: Passes the conditional generalization screen only if the Q=3 grid minimum is not at a grid edge and lies inside the closed training interval. Otherwise the generalization claim is rejected.
Uses the identical conditional screen as H1 and is reported as a comparator, not as an EMRF claim.

numerical_gate.convergence_requirement: For every galaxy, acceleration-grid value, scan direction, and law, at least one declared optimizer start must return a successful finite result. A failed individual start does not invalidate the fit when another declared start succeeds, but successful and failed start counts must be reported. No successful finite start makes the confirmatory result incomplete and invalid.

required: complete included galaxy names and counts
criterion result for every registered hypothesis
forbidden: changing thresholds after viewing Q=3 outcomes
interpreting Delta Q equals 1 as calibrated significance
using BIC from the penalized objective
promoting this same-catalogue challenge to independent replication
